claims.claim: Hobb proposes a test in which the reader of a passage of dialogue should be able to tell who is speaking without the attribution tags.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, speaking on Writing Excuses 11.Bonus-01 (Oct 2016), fan transcript at wetranscripts
claims.quote: able to tell who is talking without all the little clues

claims.claim: Hobb says that what an assassin notices on entering a room differs from what a child entering the same room notices.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, speaking on Writing Excuses 11.Bonus-01 (Oct 2016), fan transcript at wetranscripts
claims.quote: if you are an assassin and you walk into the room

claims.claim: Hobb says the biographical details filled in around a character build the world at the same time.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, speaking on Writing Excuses 11.Bonus-01 (Oct 2016), fan transcript at wetranscripts
claims.quote: details that fill in around the character build the world

claims.claim: Elliott describes the first paragraph of Assassin's Apprentice as an excerpt from a piece being composed inside the story's own world.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, 'A Robin Hobb Rereading Series-Entry 1', Elliott RWI, 2019
claims.quote: an excerpt from a piece being composed within the milieu

claims.claim: Elliott names Hobb's habit of opening chapters with in-world reference materials an Asimovian move.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, 'A Robin Hobb Rereading Series: Entry 226', Elliott RWI, 2021
claims.quote: the Asimovian move of grounding chapters in in-milieu reference materials

claims.claim: Elliott, writing as a medievalist, says the chapter-opening passage enacts the piecing-together of disparate and not always complete sources.
claims.source: Geoffrey B. Elliott, 'A Robin Hobb Rereading Series: Entry 226', Elliott RWI, 2021
claims.quote: the piecing-together of disparate and not always complete sources

claims.claim: The reviewer says Hobb takes a cliched epic-fantasy plot point and fleshes it out with motivations and characters and consequences until it looks realistic.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'The Golden Fool, by Robin Hobb', 2013
claims.quote: fleshes it out with motivations and characters and consequences

claims.claim: The reviewer says Hobb tells a standard heroic plot from an unexpected, peripheral perspective and thereby gives the realistic inner workings of the myth.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'The Golden Fool, by Robin Hobb', 2013
claims.quote: the realistic inner workings of the myth

claims.claim: The reviewer identifies worrying about the apprentice fees for dependants as the kind of domestic matter most epic fantasy does not spend pages on.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'The Golden Fool, by Robin Hobb', 2013
claims.quote: worrying about the apprentice fees for dependants

claims.claim: The reviewer says the book insists that motivations are personal and that consequences will also be personal.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'The Golden Fool, by Robin Hobb', 2013
claims.quote: that motivations are personal, and that consequences will also be personal

claims.feature: other: fantastic subordinated to the ordinary
claims.claim: The reviewer says the book reminds the reader that the fantasy only matters because of the reality in its shadow.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'The Golden Fool, by Robin Hobb', 2013
claims.quote: the fantasy only matters because of the reality in its shadow

claims.claim: The reviewer says Hobb builds tense scenes out of characters watching each other's expressions, so that much is accomplished with only glances.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'The Golden Fool, by Robin Hobb', 2013
claims.quote: So much can be accomplished with only glances

claims.claim: The reviewer judges that Hobb's prose is usually unremarkable, locating her effect elsewhere than in sentence beauty.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'Dragon Keeper, by Robin Hobb', 2014
claims.quote: As is usually the case with Hobb, her prose is unremarkable

claims.claim: The reviewer judges Hobb's prose solid and effective and occasionally pretty, but not award-winning for beauty.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'Fool's Fate, by Robin Hobb', 2013
claims.quote: prose is solid and effective and occasionally pretty

claims.claim: The reviewer describes Hobb's language as having a slightly heavy and old-fashioned tone common to the genre.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel (pseudonymous reviewer), 'Fool's Quest, by Robin Hobb', 2015
claims.quote: that slightly heavy and old-fashioned tone common to the genre
